n: David, speaking as king, promises to sing of covenant love and justice — the two qualities a godly ruler must reflect.
David resolves to live with integrity, even in private, at home. His question ‘When will you come to me?’ shows he longs for God’s presence.

f.g: Blameless, whole, with integrity — not flawless.

n: He will not look at anything worthless or wicked, and won’t let the deeds of those who turn from God stick to him. Guarding what we look at guards the heart.

f.w: no wicked thing before mine eyes

n: A twisted, perverse heart will have no place in him, and he will not be intimate with evil.
As king he will remove anyone who secretly slanders others, and will not put up with arrogance.
He will seek out the faithful to be his companions and officials. Good leaders choose good counselors.
Liars and deceivers will have no place in the king’s household or court.
‘Early’ means ‘every morning,’ when kings held court. He promises daily vigilance to keep Jerusalem, God’s city, free of evildoers.

f.g: Morning by morning — when judgment was given at the city gate.
